title: Sampled operational profile catalog and graceful deprecation flow
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Define and implement a lightweight sampled operational profile catalog that supplements existing verified performance profiles with production-derived signals, and establish a graceful deprecation & republish flow for pinned versions.

Scope:
- Design a sampling strategy that uses shadow production traffic (1-5%) to capture real-world latency/throughput/cost distributions for newly onboarded models and significant model-version updates.
- Store sampled manifests in the operational profile catalog with metadata: sample window, hardware region, sequence-length percentiles, token-cost estimate, and observed p95/p99 latency.
- Create a publish SLA and a refresh schedule: initial sampled verification within 72h of onboarding, weekly sample-driven staleness checks for first 30 days, then monthly for stable pins.
- Implement deprecation windows: soft-deprecate (notify owners, surface in Console) -> hard-deprecate (prevent new pins) -> archive (remove from default catalog) with TTL and rollback-safe republish.
- Define observability contract (dashboard + alerts) for drift in latency/cost beyond defined thresholds that will trigger automated re-validation and canary rollouts.
- Define guardrails for when sampled signals can override or trigger republishing of a Redwood-verified profile versus when manual steward signoff is required.

Out-of-scope for this ticket: full auto-pinning of model variants and region-aware per-customer optimization (follow-up work).
acceptance_criteria: A sampled operational profile entry is created after shadowing a model version and includes sequence length percentiles, p50/p95/p99 latency, observed throughput, and a normalized cost estimate.
Console surfaces sampled profile alongside the canonical verified profile and marks the sample window and sample rate.
A refresh scheduler runs and flags profiles that exceed staleness thresholds; flagged profiles create a Slack/Email alert to owners and an automatic canary job to re-verify under controlled traffic.
Deprecation flow can be initiated from Console (soft/hard/archive) and creates a clear audit trail and rollback links to prior verified profile artifacts.
Playbook page (Confluence) links from the ticket and contains runbooks for investigating drift and republishing profiles.
Benchmarks captured by sampling are available to engineers as CSV export and as time-series metrics in Grafana for 90 days.

2025-02-24 — Marco Alvarez: Engineering notes: we prefer a phased rollout: (1) internal canary on staging, (2) 0.5% shadow on a small customer set, (3) widen to 1-3% for diverse traffic types. Need feature flagging and per-region opt-in. Open question: how to account for tokenization differences across languages — suggested adding locale tags to samples.

Key UX decisions: show sampled confidence interval, sample window, and a one-click 'request reverify' action. UX asks for a compact badge to indicate 'sampled' vs 'verified'.
